messages:
alex_sales: Hey team — Orchid Health sent back the SIG focusing on BCP/DR. They're asking for RTO/RPO numbers, backup cadence, failover behavior, retention, and who gets access during a DR. Can we draft concise answers for the form?

maria_se: I can take a pass. Confirming this is for our Hosted API only, right? Not Dedicated/Private.
alex_sales: Correct — Hosted only for now.
maria_se: Draft bullets for the SIG free-text response:
- Availability SLA: 99.9% monthly for hosted inference endpoints.
- Traffic failover: Active routing with cross-region fallback; automated routing change target <= 2 minutes.
- RTO: Target for automated recovery paths (routing and capacity remap) <= 2 minutes; full service recovery target <= 4 hours depending on incident class.
- RPO: Persistent metadata (configs, model pins, audit logs) RPO <= 1 hour. Transient inference caches (KV/prefix cache) are not durable and may be lost during failover.
- Backups: Nightly full backups of persistent metadata + hourly incremental snapshots to an encrypted multi-region object store.
- Retention: Default backup retention 90 days (longer retention available as a paid option).
- Restore: Target initiation of restore within 4 hours of an authorized request; completion time depends on dataset size.
- Operator access: Access limited to authorized SREs and on-call operators, governed by an approval process and fully audited. Key material is managed via customer or Redwood KMS/HSM where applicable.

tim_security: A couple of clarifications to keep things defensible in a vendor risk review:
- Avoid phrasing like "near-zero" RPO for anything we can't guarantee. Use explicit buckets (<= 1 hour for persistent; transient caches not persisted).
- For SLA math: state that downtime excludes scheduled maintenance and customer-side networking. SLA credits are pro-rata per incident per contract terms.

maria_se: Reworded one-paragraph answer for SIG text field:
"Redwood's hosted inference service offers a 99.9% monthly availability SLA. We operate active routing with cross-region fallback; automated routing changes are targeted within 2 minutes while full service recovery timelines depend on incident severity (target <= 4 hours). Persistent customer metadata (configs, model pins, audit logs) are protected with nightly full backups and hourly incremental snapshots to an encrypted multi-region object store (RPO <= 1 hour). Ephemeral inference caches are not durable and may be lost during failover. Backups are retained 90 days by default with extended retention available. Restore initiation for hosted customers is targeted within 4 hours of an approved request; final completion varies by dataset size. Operator access during DR events is limited to authorized SRE personnel, all access is logged, and keys are handled by KMS/HSM where applicable. Quarterly DR drills and annual full-recovery tests are performed; summaries can be provided for vendor reviews."

jenna_pm: Recommend we attach evidence: latest DR drill summary + backup policy + SLA doc. Prospects want supporting artifacts.

ops_bot: DR drill report uploaded: https://internal.redwood/reports/dr/2026-q1-summary (sha256: def456) :white_check_mark:

alex_sales: Good. Two quick asks from the buyer: 1) "How long do you keep backups for legal/regulatory requirements?" 2) "During a failover, can we expect reads to continue or will in-flight requests possibly fail?"

tim_security: Answer ideas:
- Retention: default 90 days; custom retention/archival is available under enterprise SLAs for compliance use cases.
- Read behavior: During cross-region failover we strive for seamless reroute; however, in-flight inference requests relying on ephemeral caches may be retried or dropped depending on client retry logic. Persistent operational metadata remains available. Recommend customers implement client-side retries with idempotency where needed.

maria_se: I'll append a short FAQ line: "Default retention for backups is 90 days; extended retention or cold-archival storage can be arranged under contract. During automatic failover we route traffic to healthy regions; most requests succeed, but transient inference state is not durable—clients should implement retries."

alex_sales: Perfect. Maria — please paste the one-paragraph SIG answer into the form, attach the DR report and backup policy links, and ping Tim for a security sign-off before I send it.
maria_se: Will do. Ping me if they push for Dedicated/Private since the numbers change.
tim_security: I'll review quickly once it's in. Note: for Dedicated/Private deployments we can provide tighter RTO/RPO and custom restore SLAs in the contract.

alex_sales: Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops_bot: Legal review request created: LR-8120 (assignee: tim_security)
